SimonGMT supplies GeometricCurrentOn.massOn (an sSup of ofReal over massAdmissibleOn), mass := massOn U, le_massOn and covectorEuclideanNorm_neg.

rationale:
Split into two children. Both reuse comparator-accepted declarations whose frozen types are byte-identical, so the split creates no new proof obligations. The selected node keeps only a short assembly, and that assembly has already been compiled.

Why split. The supplied proof (steps 1–5) chains three different kinds of argument:
(i) step 1, a supremum argument for Simon's mass, M(A − B) ≤ M(A) + M(B);
(ii) steps 3–4, a purely combinatorial recursive construction (nested infinite index sets, then a diagonal choice);
(iii) steps 2 and 5, current algebra and arithmetic in [0, ∞].
(i) and (ii) are reusable textbook lemmas, and the DAG has already proved them as Submission.cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le and Submission.cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq. Both have status accepted with all proof gates passed; their candidate commits are ea5c1199 and b046f226, both sorry-free and using only the standard axioms. This node's proof base, 648bae63, is the bare contract, so accepted declarations from other branches reach it only through DAG edges. Without the split the leaf would have to re-prove about 60 lines of accepted code inline. Linking the accepted declarations removes that duplication and isolates the only recursive construction. The twin node dimred_mbl_fc_cauchy_subseq was split the same way, reusing these declarations, and its audit was acceptable with no required changes.

Mapping onto the supplied proof.
- mass_sub_le is step 1, stated for an arbitrary support region G; that is the reused frozen type. The parent uses G = U, since M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U by definition.
- diagonal_subseq is steps 3–4, with the relation Q_r(j) = Q_r(l) abstracted to an arbitrary C r j l. The supplied J_r is the child's I_{r+1}.
- The parent keeps step 2, the pigeonhole of step 3, and step 5. For (IMC)(c) it uses the selected node's existing resolved dependency im_calculus: Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (accepted), third conjunct. This is exactly the "Tool" named in the supplied proof. Accepted precedent such as zero_dim_minimizer_zero shows that a decomposed parent's assembly may use its own depends_on.

Parent assembly.
1. Put ε_r := (2⁻¹)^(r+1) > 0 (ENNReal.pow_pos, ENNReal.inv_pos, ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top). Choose a finite 𝒬_r and, for every j, Q_r(j) ∈ 𝒬_r and IM currents R_r(j), S_r(j) with X_j(ω) − Q_r(j)(ω) = ∂R_r(j)(ω) + S_r(j)(ω) for all ω and M(R_r(j)) + M(S_r(j)) < ε_r.
2. Apply diagonal_subseq with C r j l :⇔ Q_r(j) = Q_r(l). Its hypothesis is the pigeonhole of step 3. For an infinite I, I ⊆ ⋃_{q ∈ 𝒬_r} {j ∈ I : Q_r(j) = q}. If every fibre were finite, I would be finite (Set.Finite.biUnion), so some fibre J ⊆ I is infinite, and Q_r(j) = q = Q_r(l) for all j, l ∈ J. The lemma gives a StrictMono θ with Q_r(θ(r+1)) = Q_r(θ(r)) for every r.
3. Fix r and put R := R_r(θ(r+1)) − R_r(θ(r)) and S := S_r(θ(r+1)) − S_r(θ(r)). Both are IM by (IMC)(c), since U is open. By definition (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply and the contract Sub), ∂R(ω) = R_r(θ(r+1))(dω) − R_r(θ(r))(dω) and S(ω) = S_r(θ(r+1))(ω) − S_r(θ(r))(ω). The two decompositions share the same centre, so subtracting them gives X_{θ(r+1)}(ω) − X_{θ(r)}(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω) by linear arithmetic.
4. By mass_sub_le with G = U and add_add_add_comm:
   M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R_r(θ(r+1))) + M(S_r(θ(r+1)))) + (M(R_r(θ(r))) + M(S_r(θ(r)))) ≤ ε_r + ε_r = (2⁻¹)^r.
   The last equality uses pow_succ, mul_add and ENNReal.inv_two_add_inv_two.

Verification. Scratch files are under /tmp/dor-cauchy-decomp, outside the repo.
- Both child lean_statements are byte-identical to the dag.json types of the accepted nodes and pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement. Both compile as comparator challenges in the scope replayed by gmt-compare.contract_scope: import GMT.Ch07.Submission, namespace GMT.Ch07, and the contract's opens.
- I compiled a conditional assembly with lake env lean. Its hypotheses are the two child types and the im_calculus type, and its conclusion is byte-for-byte the selected frozen type. It compiles; #print axioms gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
- The only Sub instance on GeometricCurrentOn is the contract's GMT.Ch07.instSubGeometricCurrentOnEuclid. The reused types use this same instance.
- An independent adversarial reviewer with fresh context returned ACCEPT. It re-checked byte identity and accepted status and recompiled the assembly. It also compiled an end-to-end file: the accepted child proofs verbatim plus the assembly proving Submission.dor_lmb_fc_cauchy_subseq at its exact type. That file had 0 errors and used only the standard axioms.

Alternatives rejected.
- Reusing the accepted Submission.cmc_fc_cauchy_subseq would leave a child equivalent to the parent up to formulation: current equalities, ≤ η, and an explicit (IMC)(c) premise. It would also bypass the supplied steps 1–5.
- Adding cmc_fc_cs_close_of_common_center would need pointwise ↔ current-equality conversions in both directions and saves nothing.
- Re-listing im_calculus as a child is redundant, because it is already this node's resolved dependency.

Structural checks.
- Neither child has dependencies, so the graph stays acyclic.
- Depth 4 is below the limit of 6.
- No child restates the parent or an ancestor, and the split does not solve another node.
- Each name is owned only by its accepted node, with an identical type.

subproblems.title: Mass of a difference: M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) (reuse of the accepted declaration cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U, G ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P; neither is assumed open) and all currents A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n): M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) in [0, ∞]. Here A − B is the contract subtraction, (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω), and M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) = max(X(ω), 0) over the forms ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) admissible for M_G, i.e. with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U n G). For G = U this is M(A − B) ≤ M(A) + M(B), step 1 of the supplied proof. This is, with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.flat_convergence-a1.cauchy_subseq-a1.mass_sub_le-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (A - B).massOn G ≤ A.massOn G + B.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 ("Mass of a difference") of the supplied proof of dor_lmb_fc_cauchy_subseq (Simon Ch. 6, 2.5, chapter-06.txt line 231: M_W(T) = sup{T(ω) : |ω| ≤ 1, spt ω ⊆ W}; this subadditivity makes the d_W of 7.1, line 2020, pseudometrics), stated for an arbitrary support region G in place of U. The same statement, with the byte-identical frozen type, is already the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le, whose Lean proof follows these steps; the proof is nevertheless given in full.
1. (Reduction to one form.) By definition M_G(A − B) = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n G}. By the least-upper-bound property of the supremum in [0, ∞] (sSup_le) it suffices to prove ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for every admissible ω. Fix an admissible ω: ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
2. (−ω is admissible.) TestFormOn U n is a real submodule of the differential n-forms, so −ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, with underlying form x ↦ −ω(x) (Submodule.coe_neg, Pi.neg_apply). Pointwise negation does not change the topological support, so tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω ⊆ G (tsupport_neg). The Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under negation of the covector, since its coefficients only change sign before being squared (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg); hence covectorEuclideanNorm(−ω(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x. So −ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n G.
3. (Splitting the evaluation.) By the contract Sub instance the linear functional underlying A − B is A.toCurrent − B.toCurrent, so (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) by definition. The functional underlying B is linear, so B(−ω) = −B(ω) (LinearMap.map_neg). Therefore (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω).
4. (Subadditivity of ofReal.) For real s, t one has ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t), i.e. max(s + t, 0) ≤ max(s, 0) + max(t, 0) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). With step 3, ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) + ENNReal.ofReal(B(−ω)).
5. (Each term is bounded by a mass.) Each admissible form bounds the corresponding supremum from below (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since ω is admissible, ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ M_G(A); since −ω is admissible (step 2), ENNReal.ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_G(B). Adding these (add_le_add) and using step 4 gives ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B).
6. (Conclusion.) Step 5 holds for every admissible ω, so by step 1, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). For G = U, where M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U by definition, this is M(A − B) ≤ M(A) + M(B). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce the supremum bound to a single admissible form ω (sSup_le).
−ω is admissible: same tsupport (tsupport_neg) and same coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
(A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω) by the contract Sub instance and linearity of B.
ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, then le_massOn for ω (with A) and for −ω (with B); conclude with sSup_le.

subproblems.title: Diagonal extraction from nested infinite index sets (reuse of the accepted declaration cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq)
subproblems.statement: Let C : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop be any family of binary relations C r on ℕ. Suppose that for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite set I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite set J ⊆ I such that C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ J. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ. These are steps 3–4 of the supplied proof with the pigeonhole relation Q_r(j) = Q_r(l) replaced by an arbitrary relation. This is, with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.flat_convergence-a1.cauchy_subseq-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (C : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop), (∀ (r : ℕ) (I : Set ℕ), I.Infinite → ∃ J ⊆ I, J.Infinite ∧ ∀ j ∈ J, ∀ l ∈ J, C r j l) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ r, C r (φ (r + 1)) (φ r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 ("Nested infinite index sets" and "Diagonal choice") of the supplied proof of dor_lmb_fc_cauchy_subseq (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, chapter-06.txt lines 2101–2105: "apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}} … d(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}"). The relation "Q_r(j) = Q_r(l)" of the supplied proof is replaced by an arbitrary relation C r j l, and the supplied J_r is I_{r+1} below. The same statement, with the byte-identical frozen type, is already the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_fc_cs_diagonal_subseq, whose Lean proof follows these steps; the proof is nevertheless given in full.
1. (Choice of refinements.) By the hypothesis and the axiom of choice there is a function F that assigns to every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite I ⊆ ℕ a set F(r, I) with F(r, I) ⊆ I, F(r, I) infinite, and C r j l for all j, l ∈ F(r, I).
2. (Nested index sets.) Put I_0 := ℕ, which is infinite, and recursively I_{r+1} := F(r, I_r). By induction on r every I_r is infinite, so F is only applied to infinite sets and the recursion is well defined. By step 1, for every r, I_{r+1} ⊆ I_r and C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ I_{r+1}.
3. (Unboundedness.) An infinite set of natural numbers contains elements above every bound (Set.Infinite.exists_gt). Hence for every r and every a ∈ ℕ we may choose g(r, a) ∈ I_{r+1} with a < g(r, a).
4. (Diagonal choice.) Define φ recursively by φ(0) := g(0, 0) and φ(r + 1) := g(r + 1, φ(r)). Then φ(0) ∈ I_1 and φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+2}, so φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} for every r. Moreover φ(r) < g(r + 1, φ(r)) = φ(r + 1) for every r, so φ is strictly increasing (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ; by induction on k ≥ 1, φ(r) < φ(r + k)).
5. (Consecutive terms are related.) Fix r. By step 4, φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1}, and φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+2} ⊆ I_{r+1} by step 2. Both lie in I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r), so step 1 with j = φ(r + 1) and l = φ(r) gives C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give a strictly increasing φ with C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)) for every r ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose refinements F(r, I) ⊆ I that are infinite and pairwise C r-related.
Nested infinite sets I_0 = ℕ, I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r): I_{r+1} ⊆ I_r and I_{r+1} is pairwise C r-related.
Diagonal choice φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} with φ(r) < φ(r + 1) (Set.Infinite.exists_gt); φ is StrictMono.
φ(r), φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r) gives C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)).
